{{Quote|I just happen to have a chance-cube here. Blue&mdash;it's the boy. Red&mdash;his mother.|Watto, deciding whether to wager Anakin or Shmi Skywalker in a bet|<ref name="TPM" />}}
'''Watto's chance cube''' was the personal [[Chance cube/Legends|chance cube]] owned by [[Watto/Legends|Watto]], a [[Toydarian/Legends|Toydarian]] [[Junk dealer/Legends|junk dealer]] living on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]].<ref name="TPM" /> A six-sided chance cube, the faces of Watto's cube were colored red and blue<ref name="CCG-Chance" /> and was loaded in his favor.<ref name="VD">''[[Star Wars: Episode I: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> In [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]],<ref name="TEC">''[[The Essential Chronology (real-world book)|The Essential Chronology]]'' established the events of {{Film|I}} to have occurred in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]].</ref> Watto was challenged to a wager by [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] to release his [[Slavery/Legends|slaves]], [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin]] and [[Shmi Skywalker Lars/Legends|Shmi Skywalker]]. Unwilling to lose both of his slaves, Watto insisted that the wager decide the fate of only one of them. When Jinn asked for Anakin to be freed, Watto insisted they let fate decide and rolled his chance cube. If it came up blue, then Anakin would be freed. If it was red, Shmi. Despite the cube being weighted in Watto's favor, Jinn used [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] to alter the roll to his desired outcome.<ref name="TPM" />
